summary: Sandstone light at the entrance to Mobjack Bay, Virginia, first lit 1805; keepers to 1919, acetylene that year, decommissioned 1963; county-owned, tower closed, relit 2021.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends and the Mathews County Historical Society give 17 January 1805 as the first lighting; the record's 1804 matches the tower's construction and the USLHS establishment date rather than the first light. The 1973 nomination says the light was first put into use in 1806 (see resolved_conflicts and notes_for_editor).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The tower was built between March and November 1804 (LighthouseFriends); the state register says it was completed in 1805 and the nomination says completed by 1805 and first put into use in 1806; the first lighting is 17 January 1805 (LighthouseFriends, Historical Society). The 1804 and 1805 dates are construction and first lighting; the 1806 first-use date in the nomination is a disagreement the story states and does not resolve.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) First lighting: LighthouseFriends and the Historical Society say 17 January 1805; the state register says completed 1805; the nomination says completed by 1805 and first put into use in 1806 (a clean passage: 'The light was completed by 1805, and it was first put into use in 1806, the year that Burroughs received his final payment'). The USLHS 'established' date is 1804. (2) Island size and shape: LighthouseFriends quotes the 1801 survey (about 100 acres; 'an Island separated from the main land by a creek'); the Historical Society says the island was 200+ acres originally; the 1973 nomination says that when the light was built the point was a peninsula joined to the mainland, and that it is now an island of about one-third acre. The story states the nomination's and LighthouseFriends's versions and does not choose. (3) Electrification: 1950 (LighthouseFriends) vs 1960 (Historical Society). (4) Deed to county: 1976 (LighthouseFriends) vs 1975 (Historical Society); the state register gives no year. (5) 1963: LighthouseFriends says replaced by a lighted buoy; the state register says a new light on piers to the south. (6) Height: LighthouseFriends 58 ft; station record 18.0 m; roster page shows a tower height of 56 ft. (7) The 1919 Bulletin list (PDF p. 39) is OCR-garbled at the entry ('New Point Comfort, Va., oil Sep tember 15, 1919'). The story claims only the date and that it is a change; it does not say what changed. The entry was found in a list, not a column table, so no column-position match was made; the page image was not viewed. (8) Bulletin index 'change in illuminant 95' gives the Bulletin's printed page 95, not confirmed. (9) Corpus pages: the 1894 repairs list is on scan p. 427 (the OCR page index marks the printed page '102?', unconfirmed) and the 1896-97 entry 507 is on scan p. 101 (confirmed by corpus page search). (10) The National Register nomination (73002037) is not digitised on NPGallery; the Virginia nomination is an OCR with letter spacing, so the story quotes only passages whose letters are spaced exactly as the cached text prints them. (11) USCG history pages were blocked (403 via Internet Archive). (12) No newspaper searches run for this station. (13) Roster matched to the USLHS place by name and position (0.37 km); person slugs come from roster.py; the roster lines in the story were checked against the archive page. (14) The Light Attendant heading for Henry L. Dow is the USLHS's; role 'other'. (15) Farley: LighthouseFriends says one of the few known African Americans to receive an official appointment; the Historical Society says 'one of the few ... officially appointed African-American keepers'; the petition is undated in LighthouseFriends. (16) The nomination gives the construction agreement as $8,750 ('For eight thousand, seven hundred fifty dollars, Burroughs was to produce ...'); LighthouseFriends reports a $5,000 appropriation and an extra $3,500, which is not the same sum. The story states both.
